articles.title: Keith Andrews exclusive: Brentford head coach on the improvements he hopes can help the Bees 'break the ceiling' and reach Europe
articles.summary: Sky Sports exclusive: After Brentford missed out on a place in Europe in the final seconds of the 2025/26 Premier League season, head coach Keith Andrews discusses planning how the Bees can take the next step this season
articles.body:
They were drawing 1-1 with Liverpool at Anfield and knew that one goal would be enough to finish seventh and secure Europa League football.

In the 10th minute of added time, Mikkel Damsgaard dropped the ball off to Vitaly Janelt on the left-hand side of the penalty area. The midfielder hit a cross first time that curled in the most inviting way to the centre of the box.

Kevin Schade was waiting for it, but Dango Ouattara got there first - and steered it off target.

Keith Andrews put his head in his hands and sank to his knees. His first season as a head coach had nearly ended in the most perfect way.

"I felt that epitomised the journey we'd been on last season, with how we started the season, how we grew into the season," he says, reflecting on that moment just over three months on.

"Everybody was so engrossed in our journey and gave absolutely everything. There was no shame at all from not getting into Europe, but it whetted the appetite pretty nicely for how we would do things going into pre-season.

"I sat on holiday and had a chance to think about things with immense pride at what we'd achieved. The next thought, very quickly, was how and where we go again."

Speaking to Sky Sports that day, he promised improvement in 2026/27. "This is a baseline," he said. "We'll continue to push hard."

Around a fortnight after that Sunday at Anfield, Andrews was back at base.

"There's amazing thinking time you don't normally get on a weekly basis to plan and look at things in a more forensic way," he says.

"You look to improve how we train, how we prepare, what the squad feels like, what the dynamic feels like. Everything where you feel we can get a little bit better.

"I felt like we didn't need huge meetings about what this season will be, I just felt it was there day-to-day. You could smell it, you could feel it."

The first major change came on June 12 with the appointment of his former Republic of Ireland team-mate Damien Duff as his assistant.

"He's an unbelievable support for me on a daily basis. You've got to be very impactful in your role and whatever responsibilities you have and Damien is certainly that."

The squad planning stage came next and, after an intense summer in 2025, this one was a lot less so.

Star players Bryan Mbeumo and Christian Norgaard were sold to Manchester United and Arsenal respectively, while Yoane Wissa's eventual departure to Newcastle was protracted and disruptive.

There were no headline sales this year. In fact, the only first-team exits were those of Ethan Pinnock - who only played four times in the Premier League last season - and Frank Onyeka - who had spent the best part of two seasons away from west London - to Coventry for less than £12m.

"At certain stages last season, we just lacked that little bit at senior experience in the squad, different options within games to change it," Andrews says.

"We always try to find a way of competing and our players gave absolutely everything last season, but at times they probably needed a little bit more help.

"The way we've gone about our transfers this summer has been very precise. Jannik [Schuster] is a centre-back with a younger age profile and has slotted into the club really well, Callum Wilson and Jaidon Anthony have proven Premier League quality with experience, so it's not just on the pitch, it's off it in terms of what they bring.

"Mamadou Sangare was an eye-catching signing and he's started really well in our shirt. And the latest one is Malick [Diouf] from West Ham, who we were delighted to be able to get into the building.

"We've added to an already really good squad, we've added very well and we've kept hold of exactly who we wanted to keep hold of. I'm really, really happy with the deals we've got done."

Andrews often speaks about getting better - and is open about the fact that getting better than last season means reaching Europe: "Naturally, the next step for us is to try and break that ceiling."

He will, no doubt, field questions on that topic in press conferences for many months to come.

"The next level of development of individuals," he says.

"Pick a player… Michael Kayode. He had an amazing season, let's get him better. You make all your players better, you feed them that confidence, you create that environment, which we do create. It's inevitable if someone is as humble and hungry as Michael, they will get better.

"Players getting better naturally improves the team. Then you look at each phase of the game.

"At set-pieces we look a real threat, we look really dominant at the moment and we want to continue that.

"How do we create chances? The game is about scoring at one end and keeping goals out at the other, so how do you create opportunities? We want to create opportunities in different ways and not just be a predictable team that can only do it one way.

"And how do we become better without the ball? Are we pressing aggressively high? Can we sit in deep and absorb pressure and be a transition threat, but defend our box with aggression and collective spirit?

"They are just some examples about how we want to take the next step."

So far, that next step is beginning to take shape.

On the opening weekend, they welcomed Tottenham to the Gtech Community Stadium - and blew Roberto De Zerbi's side away.

They won 3-0, but it would have been four had Igor Thiago not rolled his penalty onto the base of the left-hand post.

Analysing the game afterwards, Sky Sports ' Jamie Redknapp was impressed by what he saw.

"When somebody was out of position, they just found a way to fill the right areas. They are incredibly brave at the back, the two centre-backs play so high and press you, stop you getting out," he said.

"What Roberto De Zerbi said beforehand was that they were going to deal with a lot of long balls today, but what they actually dealt with was total football.

"It can mean different things when I hear that said," Andrews responds.

"When I think about that in terms of how we play the game, we can play in different ways. We can control games now with the ability we have as a team, the quality we have technically as a team.

"The individuals are flourishing within the squad and how we're playing, then if teams want to have a fight, we'll have a fight.

"We've got so many different attributes within the squad where we can cause the opposition problems in an unpredictable way, but we always respect every phase of the game and try and respect the opposition where we try to nullify their strengths and see if we can outdo them."

It was an evening to remember for Andrews.

"Firstly, we need to start with the fans. I thought the flags [organised by fan group TW8 Casuals] and the energy as the players came in from their warm-up and pre-game was pretty special.

"It felt energetic, it felt edgy. I loved the intentions of our fans straightaway in that game. I felt they could sense us producing a performance.

"I was confident the players would. You never truly know. I thought the connection between the players and the fans was really special and we maintained it throughout."

A 6-1 thumping of Birmingham in the Carabao Cup followed, before a 1-1 draw against Leeds at Elland Road last weekend, during which he felt Schade should have been awarded a penalty after a trip by Jayden Bogle in the box.

Sunderland's visit to the capital is up next on Saturday afternoon.

"We're in a good place, there's no denying that. The players are playing freely, with a lot of verve and personality, which I really like.

"The only way you keep that going is keeping striving, keeping pushing each other, being very demanding of each other. It's a good place to be demanding of each other when you play so well and with such an edge.

"Nothing is given in this league, but we can push the group more, they can push each other to see how far we can go."

They came within one goal of Europe at Anfield. Andrews wants to make sure Brentford get even closer this time.

articles.title: Fabian Hurzeler: Brighton head coach on Europe, ambition and challenging the Premier League establishment
articles.summary: Fabian Hurzeler has made his mark at Brighton, but after two eighth-placed finishes and a summer of change, the 33-year-old believes the club can take another step with a European campaign ahead; Watch Coventry vs Brighton this Sunday live on Sky Sports, kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
"Last season we did it, maybe not through the whole season, but definitely we had a lot of great achievements," he told Sky Sports, with Brighton set to compete in Europe for only the second time in their history.

Beating Manchester City, Chelsea and Liverpool, criticising Arsenal and Mikel Arteta's style , clashing with Pep Guardiola and collecting a string of touchline bans - there has been little doubt about Hurzeler's impact over his two seasons in the Premier League.

The 33-year-old's passion in the dugout has become a defining feature of his proactive style, delivering consecutive eighth-place finishes.

It has landed him in trouble, too, but that is nothing new. At St Pauli, he once collected seven yellow cards before February.

"It definitely won't change," he said. "I want to be a winner, I want to win things for Brighton, I want to achieve together with the fans something special."

The Conference League, which begins next month, gives Brighton another opportunity to turn their recent progress into silverware. They watched rivals Crystal Palace lift the trophy in May, but for Hurzeler, the challenge is less about matching them and more about proving Albion can compete on multiple fronts.

"We have high expectations of ourselves. We want to play a season the fans will always remember, but we have to see as a club that we are capable of playing a lot of games in a very successful way," he said.

"We always [talk] of making the next step, growing as a club, and therefore we have to show now that we are capable of being successful and achieving things without losing our style and intensity."

Hurzeler now has the fourth-youngest squad in the Premier League after a busy summer in which 11 players arrived, alongside the departures of established figures including Carlos Baleba, Jan Paul van Hecke, Danny Welbeck and James Milner.

It is a changed squad, but Hurzeler believes his age gives him an advantage in getting the best out of it.

"I want to be myself, I don't want to play a role, and my age definitely helps regarding understanding the players," he said.

"I always say I speak their language and I understand their thoughts, because it wasn't that long ago when I played. I didn't play on their level, but I understand their feelings, their thoughts, maybe their doubts, their fears, what every player has."

That understanding will be important as Brighton integrate another batch of talented young signings, centre-back Luka Vuskovic already proving a smart buy at £50m from Tottenham. Hurzeler trusts the club's recruitment model to deliver again - and his staff to get the best out of them.

He has overseen a victory, a draw and a defeat in their first three Premier League games of this season, having had more big chances (15) and a higher xG (7.4) than any other side while only Arsenal (24) and Man City (26) have faced fewer shots (33).

"It's now our responsibility to really integrate these new players. They are here for a reason, and we proved in the past that we have one of the best recruitment systems in the world, so they have potential and they will show this potential."

Hurzeler was a surprise appointment when he replaced Roberto De Zerbi, but two seasons in he is no longer the unknown quantity he was when he arrived.

The demands of the Premier League have shaped him, too, from facing the best managers in the world to handling the pressure of a long season. But when things go wrong, Hurzeler looks closer to home.

"I can say that I'm a better manager now than I was before, but not only because I reflect on my mistakes; I reflect on my decisions, I reflect on my progress and my development," he said. "I have great staff around me, I have great experts, great support from all of my staff members and I have great support from my team and great personalities."

That approach was tested midway through last season, when Brighton won just once in 13 league games. Hurzeler did not look for someone else to blame.

"I'm not going home and blaming others. If we lose, it's my responsibility, and I reflect on my decisions, I reflect on the training week, so I really try to get better after every game, and that's how I do it."

He says Brighton eventually turned the run around by focusing on what they could control rather than results, maintaining their belief and demanding greater reliability from the players on the pitch.

The lesson was simple, but important for a team trying to challenge the Premier League's established order.

"In the Premier League you need to have reliability, in the Premier League you need to be really good in the small matches," Hurzeler said.

Hurzeler has committed himself to finding that consistency at Brighton, signing a new three-year contract in May. His decision was driven as much by his relationship with the club as by what he believes it can achieve.

"I see my future here, and that's why I extended the contract, because when I started here, it felt like I got integrated into a family," he said. "You don't leave your family, you want to achieve something with the family, you want to make the next step, you want to grow as a club, and therefore I want to be part of it."

He believes that the next step is still within reach.

"I still feel that the journey is not over, I still feel we are in the middle of a journey and we can achieve great things," he said. "I have this belief and now we have to show it."

articles.title: Chelsea: Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter to sell stakes in Premier League club
articles.summary: Chelsea majority owners Clearlake Capital own 61.5 per cent of club; Todd Boehly and Mark Walter own 12.8 per cent, but pair have held talks over selling shares to Clearlake, who are led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose Feliciano; Boehly was face of consortium which bought club four years ago
articles.body:
The deal paves the way for Clearlake to take full control of Chelsea, owning 86.5 per cent of the club, with Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss owning 13.5 per cent.

Boehly was the face of the consortium which bought Chelsea in 2022 but Clearlake co-founder Behdad Eghbali has become the most powerful figure at the club. Chelsea say there will be no changes to the day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the club following this transaction.

Boehly and Walter are making a small profit on their investment. Jonathan Goldstein has also stepped down from the Chelsea board, along with Boehly and Walter. They no longer have any role in Chelsea's governance, management or decision-making.

There are no plans to appoint a new chairman but the executive sporting and commercial team are remaining in place.

The UK government forced Roman Abramovich to sell Chelsea for £2.5bn, with a guarantee of £1.5bn to be invested in the club.

Boehly said: "It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club. I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

"I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the club.

"I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake's leadership."

Eghbali and Jose Feliciano , co-founders of Clearlake Capital, said in a statement: "Todd has been an important partner throughout our ownership of Chelsea, and we thank him for his time and contribution as chairman. He will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family.

"Clearlake has served as Chelsea's majority owner since 2022, and as we move to full control our focus is to continue investing in the club's infrastructure, sporting performance, player development and delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the club's supporters."

In March 2025, Boehly said Chelsea's owners could go their separate ways if they could not agree on the future of Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea bosses are considering whether to leave Stamford Bridge or to expand, with Earl's Court seen as a possible new location.

All options are being evaluated, with the project said to be complicated by the limited space in London to build.

In an interview with Bloomberg , Boehly said: "We have to think long term about what we're trying to accomplish.

"We have a big stadium development opportunity that we have to flesh out. That's going to be where we're either aligned, or we ultimately decide to go different ways."

There had been tensions too between Boehly and Clearlake in 2024.

Sky Sports News reported in September 2024 that Boehly had been unhappy with the way the club is being run and that he did not want Mauricio Pochettino to lose his job as head coach in May of that year.

Enzo Maresca replaced Pochettino and went on to win the Conference League and Club World Cup, but he left at the start of 2026, with Chelsea eventually finishing 10th and without European football.

Xabi Alonso was appointed as the new manager this summer and has the full support of the ownership.

'Boehly exit won't change Chelsea transfer strategy or ambition'

"Xabi Alonso has felt the full support of the club since he joined in July. He really enjoys the working conditions, he's very happy working with those above him and there's clear alignment with the board in terms of the strategy.

"The day-to-day running, the leadership, the strategy, that remains unchanged. This very much is a financial transaction. There's no real power shift

"In terms of the strategy, that remains very clear and unchanged. Chelsea want to be consistently challenging for silverware. They want to be at the very top of the Premier League table, challenging domestically and in Europe, and they want a period of sustained success.

"In terms of their transfer strategy, it will be very similar to what we've seen over the course of the summer. We know what happened during the first three years under Clearlake. They really targeted young players.

"Chelsea will continue to target the best young players in world football, but at the same time, they'll also look to sign players that are ready-made from the Premier League, ready-made to make an immediate impact."

'Boehly didn't have the power at Chelsea'

"Chelsea supporters have mixed feelings about Todd Boehly. Many will remember what happened in the first transfer window, when he was in charge as interim sporting director.

"They had very, very mixed fortunes, signing players like Raheem Sterling, Kalidou Koulibaly, Marc Cucurella, Wesley Fofana, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Denis Zakaria. It was not a great transfer window.

"The issue Boehly had was that although he was the figurehead of the takeover, he didn't have more than 12 and a half per cent of the shares. The majority shareholders were always Clearlake.

"And for the past few years, Behdad Eghbali, the co-founder of Clearlake, has been the most powerful person at the club.

"I'm not sure what the future holds for Boehly. He's a big investor. He's got more than 100 investments. He likes investing in sports. For instance, he's a co-owner of the LA Dodgers.

"I've just got a funny feeling that he may be back in English football before too long, because if you speak to American sports investors, they will tell you that one of the places to be is the Premier League."

articles.title: Joao Pedro reminds me of Karim Benzema and is on same level as Erling Haaland, says Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso
articles.summary: Joao Pedro was named Premier League player of the month for August after a superb start to the season for Chelsea; Xabi Alonso compared him to Karim Benzema and Erling Haaland ahead of Saturday's meeting with Hull at Stamford Bridge
articles.body:
Joao Pedro was named the Premier League's player of the month for August on Friday after contributing two goals and two assists in his first three games of the season for the Blues.

Alonso has been delighted by his impact and feels the 24-year-old, who scored 20 goals in 50 games for Chelsea last term, should be seen in the same category as his Manchester City counterpart.

"I would say yes," said Alonso when asked in his press conference if he sees him as being on the same level as Haaland.

"If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I am sure that Joao is there. So I would rate him that way.

"He has been top. Not just football-wise, personality-wise. His maturity, his desire.

"He has a very strong goal this year: to have a great season, to score many goals, and to be a nominee for not just this month but more months.

"I am not surprised, but really happy with the kind of player that we have here with Joao."

Alonso continued his praise of Joao Pedro by saying he sees similarities with his former Real Madrid team-mate Benzema, who scored 354 goals in 658 games for the Spanish side.

"In many things he reminds me of Benzema," he added. "Because he is good in the box, he is good out of the box, he is good coming to the left side, he is good with the head.

"He is very complete and he is intelligent.

"He is still young. He still has things to develop. But he has many, many absolutely outstanding qualities."

Joao Pedro's form earned him a Brazil recall this week, having been left out of Carlo Ancelotti's squad for the World Cup.

"It was painful for him," added Alonso. "But that's way back. And we are now talking about other things, like what he is doing well and what he can do better."

Chelsea front three 'complete each other'

Joao Pedro has formed part of a dangerous front three with Cole Palmer and £117m summer signing Morgan Rogers, both of whom have also starred under Alonso.

The trio have six goals and four assists in three Premier League games between them and Joao Pedro feels their qualities complement each other perfectly.

"We are very similar in the way we think," he told Sky Sports . "But also we are very different players, so I think we complete each other.

"For me, it's very good when you look behind and you have two No 10s like Cole and Morgan. I'm very happy to play with them.

"I think Cole can pass very well but also he can score. Morgan is a little bit the same.

"I think the way we think is very similar, but in the same way, I am more of a nine; I hold the ball more. Cole is more of a 10, and Morgan is more carrying the ball and dribbling."

articles.title: George Williams: England coach Brian McDermott confirms Warrington Wolves star as captain for Rugby League World Cup
articles.summary: George Williams will captain England at the upcoming Rugby League World Cup which leaves a dilemma for head coach Brian McDermott; watch Wakefield Trinity vs Leigh Leopards in the Super League Eliminators, live on Sky Sports on Friday September 18, with kick-off at 8pm
articles.body:
Williams suffered a neck injury and required surgery in April but returned to action in August and has hit the ground running for Warrington Wolves since, hoping to lead them to the Super League Grand Final.

Warrington face Hull KR in the eliminators this Saturday, live on Sky Sports , with the winner facing Wigan Warriors in the semi-finals before the Grand Final on October 3.

McDermott has been impressed with Williams' return from injury and said his "leadership has been really good".

"I didn't really know George at all. In fact, I didn't know many of the squad at all, to be fair. I've only ever shook their hands after games," he said.

"I normally shook George's hand after his team beat my team when I was at Leeds. We had a horrible record against Wigan in the regular season!

"It's been really enjoyable to get to know him. He's keen as anything and while he was injured, you could tell if anyone was coming back from injury early then it would be him.

"I'm pleased to see the form he's in now, the intent he's playing. He's not feathering about on his feet and waiting for the game to come to him, he's going and getting the game. He goes and chases the game and that's George Williams all over.

"When he first broke into first grade, we all said, 'who the hell's this guy?' Because he went and got the game, he chased the game, whether he's trying to beat the bloke opposite him or quite often coming back to the inside and finding a lazy defender. Add a few years to that and he's got a bit stronger and wiser."

Williams being captain means he will almost certainly take one of the half-back spots, which raises question marks over who will partner him.

Mikey Lewis, Jake Connor, Harry Smith and Hugo Savala are all in the mix but McDermott suggested only three will be on the plane to the World Cup, which takes place in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea from October 15 to November 15.

"Whether we take a six and a seven to back up the six and a seven that I have in mind to start, I'm still not sure," said McDermott.

"We're certainly going to take another half. We need to take another half. But if we take two halves as cover, it has an impact on how many covers we have for our outside backs, what cover we have with the back rowers, what cover we have for the other spine members as well. Some of that will be to do with form, some of that will be to do with versatility as well.

"If a guy can play in the halves, but he can also play at nine, I might favour that as well. Unsure yet. Certainly, the spine members there, it's a difficult one with the spine members.

"I've got to see them play in finals. Everyone would understand who the spine members are going to be or what other players I'm choosing from. But there's another couple out there that the finals will reveal.

"Can they handle the big occasion? Can they handle the game when there's so much on the balance? I'll certainly be taking one half as back-up. Whether I take two or not, it's dependent on the ship."

McDermott confirms England assistant coaches

McDermott also confirmed on Tuesday that Sean O'Loughlin and Paul Wellens will be his England assistant coaches for the tournament.

"We've had a lot of contact. We jump on a Teams call and we've done a tonne of phone calls, just us three together, talking about squads, talking about tactics, defensive strategies, state of the game - everything we've covered," he said.

"I shared some phone calls with Lockers (O'Loughlin) individually, as I have with Wello (Wellens), and they've been great.

"You've got to bear in mind that they've been two of the best players we've produced as a country and, arguably, they have been two of the better performers internationally that we've produced.

"No matter whether the game has been won or lost, those two have always come out of the international arena with their heads held high, so I've learned a ton off them over the last few months about rep football and international football, and the mentality towards World Cup squads and how things should be done.

"They've been very helpful and very respectful, and they're both full-time, Wello with the Cowboys and Lockers with Wigan, so I've got to be careful about texting them at 2am in the morning or 2pm in the afternoon and asking for Zoom calls.

"They're not really getting paid for it, which hasn't really been a problem for them at all. They've never mentioned it, but I've been mindful of leaning on them too much, really, but they've been great, they've been awesome."

Semi-Final 2 - Saturday 26 September, Wigan Warriors v TBC, 5.30pm KO on Sky Sports

The Super League play-offs begin on Friday September 18, live on Sky Sports, and continues all the way through until the Grand Final from Old Trafford on October 3.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest vs Coventry City: Why unusually tough start should not be used to measure Frank Lampard's side
articles.summary: Coventry City have endured a miserable return to the Premier League, but all is not lost four games in - Frank Lampard is experienced enough to know that; watch Nottingham Forest vs Coventry City live on Sky Sports Main Event on Saturday; kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
Arsenal, Man City and Brighton are among the top-flight's established elite. Brighton are currently the league's top scorers, albeit five came against Coventry last weekend. High-flying Hull City are perhaps the only outlier where achievable points were dropped.

Frank Lampard's side remain pointless and without a goal heading into matchweek five. "We went one down from a moment of quality. Welcome to the Premier League," he said after defeat to Brighton, the step up in class obviously overwhelming for a squad who could only boast five players with any meaningful Premier League experience (measured as 20+ appearances).

But the city of Coventry knows all about adversity. Supporters have felt its brute force many times since slipping out of the Premier League in 2001. Four defeats is not enough to break them. Fans at the CBS Arena on Saturday made a demonstration of defiance; they will not turn their backs having fought so hard just to be here. That helps Lampard's cause immeasurably.

Coventry are competing - but only sporadically. They are aerially dominant but seem to be losing the battle on the ground. Their press is quick and co-ordinated in some areas of the pitch and not others. They create chances but do not score. Adapting to the demands in every department will be key to survival.

The physical profile of their squad should at least ensure they will not be bullied out of this division. Becoming more bullish and imposing themselves, with the conviction that they belong, is the next step. Leeds are a relevant example to draw inspiration from.

Daniel Farke's side pressure and duel their way to victories, with success rooted largely in what they do against the ball. They are hard to beat because of it. Jamie Carragher's summary of Leeds' most recent win over Newcastle on MNF tallies with that: "Newcastle have been beaten up by a really good Premier League team."

As a newly promoted side, Coventry need to get to grips with a compact shape and be aggressive with its implementation. Stylistically, it's why the club targeted giants in the summer transfer window. Winger Loum Tchaouna was the only new recruit to arrive for a significant who stands below 6ft.

If Lampard can establish a collective robustness that meets the physical demands of this league, the absence of individual star quality should matter less. Teams who rarely get outrun or outfought are often among the survivors when May rolls around.

Creatively, the Sky Blues are better than their non-existent goal tally suggests. According to expected goals (xG) data, they should have scored four already. When analysing xGOT, which evaluates the quality of an on-target attempt, that total increases to five.

Unsurprisingly, then, it stands to reason that opposition goalkeepers have played their part in such a miserable start. Gianluigi Donnarumma kept Man City alive at the Etihad, as did Konstantinos Tzolakis in defeat to Hull. Coventry lost both games by a one-goal margin.

Despite being comprehensively beaten by Brighton after Taiwo Awoniyi was sent off, player of the match Bart Verbruggen was forced into six saves. When Lewis Dunk is scoring screamers from 30 yards, his first goal from open play at the grand age of 34, you know luck has landed elsewhere.

Coventry have conceded three goals from outside the box overall, more than any other side. That suggests an issue with pressing distances, allowing opponents too much space in striking zones, but could just as easily be explained by the increase in level and tempo. The Premier League is full of tormentors. Lewis Dunk apparently among them.

But Lampard's experience should prevent any imposter syndrome setting in. The former Chelsea midfielder knows the league intimately, as a coach and a player. He understands how unforgiving it can be and will not be downtrodden by what has already happened - most of it expected.

As he prepares his side for a trip to Nottingham Forest on Saturday, live on Sky Sports , he can point to who they have played and how they have competed in parts. There is something to be said for getting visits to the Emirates and the Etihad out of the way while the scrap for points is far less consequential.

The City Ground, however, is where potential lies. Forest are yet to score a league goal at home this season. In fact, since last Christmas, the only ever-present side with fewer home points than Forest is Spurs. Coventry travel to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium next month. Both are games with the possibility for points.

Not the moment for a crisis of confidence, then. Lampard will be hoping one win is all it takes to release his players from the harshness of the Premier League. They badly need a boost.

articles.title: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta accuses players of failing to 'respect the game' as champions suffer first defeat of season to Brighton
articles.summary: Arsenals winning start to the season came to an end as Brighton emerged 3-0 winners at the Amex Stadium; Mikel Arteta was disappointed by his sides performance on both a physical and technical level; Man City now have chance to go three points clear in the Premier League
articles.body:
Goals from Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andres consigned the champions to their heaviest Premier League loss in three years and abruptly ended their winning start to the campaign.

Arteta felt his players were found wanting in the physical battle on the south coast and also bemoaned their sloppiness on the ball as they were overwhelmed by Brighton's pressing.

"A very disappointing result and performance," he said. "Full credit to Brighton in the manner they performed and went about the game.

Latest news and rumours: Brighton | Arsenal

"They were another gear from us in the basics of the game. They were always first in the first duel, in the second actions, second balls, and they started to play from there.

"And on top of that, when we had the ball, especially in our own half, we were extremely poor technically, not respecting the game and the game principles you have to apply against a team that want to press you man to man.

"That never gives you the option to dominate and control the game in the manner you want. And then when we had big chances, we didn't put them away.

"We have to make sure we learn the lesson because this can't happen again."

Speaking in his press conference, Arteta added: "There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50-50 and it changes hands, and most of the time it was for them.

"Sometimes there were some technical errors involved that opened us up in a really difficult way, but that's something to learn.

"From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear. We put ourselves in trouble one time, two times, three times and we needed to get out of that much quicker than that. That's one of the biggest lessons that we have to take from the game."

The defeat ends a run of eight consecutive Premier League wins for Arsenal. Arteta, although critical of his side's display, called for perspective ahead of the three-week international break.

"It's not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup," he said.

"With 18 players coming back, what we've done, the way we've competed and the amount of games we've won has been remarkable.

"But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level."

It is not often that Arsenal are outfought but they could not live with Brighton's intensity and the numbers backed up Arteta's criticism.

Brighton's pressing was incredible in the first half and the Gunners couldn't match their level in the second period either.

According to Opta, the hosts won possession in the final third nine times. It is the second-highest total by any side in a Premier League game this season. It is also the most by any side against Arsenal in any game either this term or last.

Arsenal were left disorientated by the blizzard of early Brighton pressure, with summer signing Bruno Guimaraes finding it particularly difficult, and could not recover their poise.

Having smothered Arsenal with their pressing, Brighton asserted their dominance from set-pieces too, scoring their third goal from one of several dangerous corners and, ultimately, claiming revenge for their acrimonious defeat in this fixture last season.

Hurzeler: We were horrible to play against

Fabian Hurzeler savoured a "special" performance from his side as Brighton moved up to third, only two points behind Arsenal.

Their total of 16 goals is the highest by any Premier League side in the first five games of a season since Manchester City hit 19 at the beginning of the 2022/23 campaign.

"Beating the current champions and the best team in England is something special," he said.

"But it's not because the result is special, it's the performance. The boys showed real togetherness and intensity.

"They were horrible to play against and that's because we did the basic things right. Overall I was very pleased with the performance.

"I think we deserved to win. It's a moment the players and the staff can enjoy because they worked hard for this but it's also important why we had this success, because we did the basics right and we were brilliant in the duels."

articles.title: Tottenham continue downward spiral as Arsenal prove they are not perfect - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: Sky Sports' writers assess the Premier League action from Friday and Saturday as Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham all suffer embarrassing defeats...
articles.body:
This Tottenham team are not a lost cause. But being bad in both boxes is a footballing nightmare. And that is where Spurs find themselves right now. Five games, no wins. And back in the relegation zone.

Latest news and rumours: Tottenham | Aston Villa

They are wasteful in front of goal and then seemingly determined to self-destruct at the other end. Sloppy passes, poor decisions, defensive lapses - gifts being handed out to the opposition.

And Roberto De Zerbi cut a frustrated figure. He called the defending for Aston Villa's second goal "unacceptable".

You could feel the anger bubbling underneath him in his post-match press conference. The most damning admission? He didn't even speak to his players after the defeat. That tells you plenty.

What was there to say? The same mistakes keep appearing. The same problems keep costing Spurs. And now, just when the manager needs his players on the training pitch to put it right, the international break arrives. Some of them won't see De Zerbi again for more than two weeks.

This isn't a lost season. There is too much talent in this Tottenham squad for that. But talent means very little if you keep shooting yourself in the foot. Top teams don't behave like this.

And if De Zerbi doesn't get that habit out of them quickly, this project is going to become another season of humiliation. Lewis Jones

Nicolas Jackson absolutely tormented Tottenham with a brilliant mixture of silky touches and bruising physicality. He gave Spurs' centre-backs no peace, constantly offering an out-ball, protecting possession and bringing those around him into the game.

It was the kind of performance that reminded you why Chelsea saw so much in him. Jackson doesn't always get the goals his all-round game perhaps deserves, but that can sometimes disguise just how valuable he is to the team. When he is playing with this confidence, everything seems to click. The midfielders have someone to find. The wide players have someone to combine with. Runners have space to attack.

It was a proper centre-forward's performance that included the game's key goal, which doubled Villa's lead.

It was a demonstration to Tottenham of exactly what they are missing through the middle. Lewis Jones

Arsenal lost 3-0 but it should have been six. Brighton missed three big chances to add to their hefty tally. We've rarely seen this from Mikel Arteta's team.

The last time Arsenal conceded three goals in a Premier League away game was in December 2023, and the Gunners even won that game at Luton 4-3. The last time they lost by a three-goal margin was May 2023, coincidentally against Brighton.

Latest news and rumours: Brighton | Arsenal

Arsenal went the entire of 2024, 2025 and most of 2026 without doing what they did at Brighton. It was uncharacteristic display, particularly on the road - where Arsenal have accumulated more away points than any other team in the last five years.

Arteta knew that Arsenal were in trouble right from the first throw-in in the game. And the way in which Arsenal were second-best from that moment to the 95th minute, this was clearly a bad day at the office, but not part of a wider problem.

Arteta was keen to call for perspective after the game: Arsenal have won every other match this season after staggering so many late arrivals from the World Cup and suffering a fair few injuries in defence.

The last time Arsenal lost in this manner was the 2026 Carabao Cup final - after which, the tactical template of 'how to beat Arsenal' then spilled into a FA Cup exit, a loss to Bournemouth and then that defeat at Manchester City which temporarily turned the title race tide.

The lengthy international break will help, but Arsenal need to make sure this Brighton blip doesn't become wobble. Sam Blitz

Brighton have started the season in electric fashion. They are comfortably the Premier League's top scorers, who have added goals to the third-best defence in the league from last season.

Interestingly, all under Fabian Hurzeler, they have won a game against the reigning champions three seasons in a row. But when they beat Man City and Liverpool in previous years, those two clubs were already in freefall. Stopping Arsenal in their full flow makes this Brighton win the best out of the three.

What makes Brighton unique is how they respond to challenges? Lose Carlos Baleba? Chema Andres will arrive and step up. Danny Welbeck leaves and Georginio Rutter is out? Babis Kostoulas will score to get you wins over United and Arsenal.

Jack Hinshelwood is injured? Pascal Gross will get you seven goal contributions in five games. "He's like a fine wine," said Hurzeler about the German after the game. The same goes for his team. They just keep getting better and better. Sam Blitz

There is something quite endearing about Everton under David Moyes. After all the hardships of the transfer window, with the smallest squad in the division, they continue to overachieve. VAR even tried to undermine their victory over Ipswich, but they rallied to make sure it didn't matter.

Everton remain unbeaten in their opening seven games across all competitions, complete with five clean sheets. When asked if working with a small squad has actually been to his advantage, Moyes said: "We're trying to make it that way."

Their 21 shots against Ipswich were their most in a Premier League game at Hill Dickinson Stadium, but Moyes still sees plenty to improve on. "I am ratting the players like you wouldn't believe," he added. "Why are we not scoring more?"

Thierno Barry was denied what most would consider a legitimate goal by VAR, but Everton were also responsible for squandering four big chances themselves. That level of profligacy will come back to bite in certain games. And yet, you cannot help but be impressed by the way Moyes has maximised the finite tools at his disposal.

His managerial nous can take Everton further than their recruitment limitations suggested was possible. Laura Hunter

It was Newcastle's valiant defending that may have seen them over the line in their 2-1 victory against Hull, but it was their blistering first-half attack which proved the telling difference on the way to three points - especially that of Harvey Barnes.

Barnes provided two assists in just seven minutes, the earliest into a Premier League game a Newcastle player has set up mulitple goals, taking the record from Fabian Schar who managed the feat in nine minutes in that 6-1 demolition job of Tottenham in 2023.

The difference here was that Barnes was facing a resolute defence that had only conceded in one of their previous four Premier League games - not that that stopped the winger picking their locks twice in four minutes.

Latest news and rumours: Newcastle | Hull

His deft inside through-ball for Joe Willock to lash home came just four minutes before slipping in a galloping Lewis Hall on the outside of the opponents' box - but he continued to provide Newcastle a creative spark throughout the 90 minutes, whipping in teasing crosses even when his side was up against it.

Barnes now has five goal contributions in seven games across all competitions for new boss Matthias Jaissle, but was still overlooked for Thomas Tuchel's England squad, missing out to Eberechi Eze, who has not started a Premier League game for Arsenal so far this campaign. If the Englishman keeps producing game-defining performances like he has so far under Jaissle, it surely will not be long before he earns the trust of the other German manager he is eager to impress. Noah Langford

Coventry's last Premier League win before their 1-0 victory at Nottingham Forest on Saturday came 25 years ago when the Sky Blues beat Sunderland at home.

On that day in April 2001, there was no such thing as VAR, but on Coventry's return to the top flight, VAR was needed to get them over the line at the City Ground.

Latest news and rumours: Forest | Coventry

Had Igor Jesus' goal stood, it would have felt very cruel on Coventry, who were worth their victory.

They battled superbly, showed fantastic spirit and had moments of quality in attack capped off by Jay Dasilva's fine winner as goalkeeper Carl Rushworth assisted the goal.

There had been a fear Frank Lampard's side would become the basement boys after a pointless and goalless start to the season.

But on their fifth attempt, the Sky Blues showed they are Premier League material.

An away day win at the City Ground, however, is becoming far too regular an occurrence for Forest.

Among ever-present sides since the start of last season, only Tottenham have won fewer home games (3) and earned fewer home points (16) in the Premier League than Forest (4 wins, 21 points).

Forest boss Glasner believes the "heaviness of the past" is affecting the squad around home games, but this defeat was not for the want of trying.

Forest had 24 shots, their second most in a Premier League match since they returned to the division in 2022.

The upcoming three-week international break will leave Glasner searching for answers as to how to fix their home form and make their performances more clinical in front of goal. Declan Olley

For the first time this season, Chelsea were without their infamous front three of 'JP Morgan' due to Joao Pedro's injury.

Danny Welbeck started in the Brazilian's place and it was set up for the England international to do well. Brentford were Welbeck's favourite opponents in his career, with six goals in his nine previous matches against the Bees before Friday night.

But Chelsea weren't the same in attack. The new-formed attack of Welbeck, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers managed just one shot on target between them at the Gtech. They averaged three shots on target in each of their previous four league games.

Pedro is not just a goalscorer, he's a player who drops off the frontline to link up with others. He has just as managed goals as he has assist this season. Welbeck is less of a creator, more of a clinical scorer.

Xabi Alonso says Pedro's absence cannot be used as an excuse - but the Chelsea manager is surely hoping in private that he is back quickly after the international break. Sam Blitz

Brentford's best buy of the transfer window may not be Mamadou Sangare after all. Jannik Schuster has announced himself to the Premier League after his £13m move from Red Bull Salzburg.

For all of Brentford's excellent attacking play - they scored three times, Igor Thiago got off the mark for the season and Kevin Schade's two assists rubberstamped his brilliant start to the season - it was in defence where they shone just as much. They are the first team to stop Chelsea scoring this season.

Schuster was a big part of that, with some outstanding defensive numbers earning the 20-year-old Player of the Match.

His 12 clearances was twice as many as the next Brentford player, which is not bad given his first home Premier League start was up against a formidable and experienced opponents in Welbeck.

"I loved him from the second I saw him," said Keith Andrews after the win over Chelsea. "He's fearless, you could see his character from just watching clips. He's whole-hearted, he has personality and aggression. They way he truly plays, he loves defending."

Nothing is happening there at all"; Liverpool play Man City, Arsenal, Brentford and Brighton after the international break and Carragher says Wirtz should not be playing
articles.body:
Carragher criticised Wirtz during the first half of Liverpool's 1-0 win at the Vitality Stadium where he was on Sky Sports co-commentary duty. "Wirtz has been really poor again," he said. "It's just nothing. Nothing is happening there at all."

And after the game, the Sky Sports pundit claimed Wirtz will never reach the level that many people expected him to achieve at Anfield.

"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Carragher on the bonus Jamie Carragher Podcast made by Sky Sports .

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.

"But the reason I worry is, I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.

"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you. It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player, I don't."

'Iraola has decision to make - he can't be in the Man City team'

Liverpool face a crucial run of games straight after the lengthy, three-week international break. They return to a bumper fixture as Enzo Maresca's Manchester City visit Anfield on October 11, live on Sky Sports.

Andoni Iraola's side also face high-flying Brentford and Brighton in the Premier League, before hosting reigning champions Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on October 1.

In between all those games, Liverpool have Champions League tests with LASK and Villarreal, as well as a Carabao Cup fourth-round game against Chelsea.

Carragher feels Wirtz should not be in the Liverpool team to face City in that first fixture.

"I think going forward Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team," said Carragher.

"I thought this Bournemouth game was a big game for Wirtz. Because if he doesn't produce [against Bournemouth], he's then going to have a three-week break. By the time we come back, we're into October. Before you know it, it'll be Christmas in six to eight weeks, or it'll feel like we're getting to Christmas. He has to do something!

"If you go through the Premier League and think of players in his position - not just for the top teams, forget the top teams who we should be judging him against, I'm talking about normal Premier League players in the middle of the table - who have done more for their clubs.

"I think of Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall at Everton. No one out there would say Dewsbury-Hall is a better player than Wirtz, or would go for more money than Wirtz, or would cost £120m. But every three or four weeks he scores a goal.

"I watched Morgan Gibbs-White for Nottingham Forest last week at Aston Villa, and in the second half he put in a performance in 45 minutes that Florian Wirtz has never done before for Liverpool.

"I've seen a goal Emiliano Buendia scored for Aston Villa at Tottenham. Again, these players aren't going to get over £100m, or £120m, but they're still giving their clubs bits every few weeks.

"Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home, for me, he can't be in the team.

"The things I've liked so far about Iraola, he's had the courage to make big decisions. Ryan Gravenberch has just signed a hefty contract on a five-year deal on massive money, because they thought him and Szoboszlai were going to be the future of the midfield going forward. He's not playing.

"Now, I can imagine the guys at the top of the club looking at that, thinking we've just given him a hefty contract. But no, he's not playing.

"The full-back situation, he keeps changing the full-backs, he's dropped Jeremie Frimpong straight away. Milos Kerkez has been in and out. So he's made decisions.

"But sooner or later he's going to have to make a decision on Florian Wirtz, and, for me, I hope it's sooner. Not because I don't like Florian Wirtz, I'm desperate for the kid to do well. I just want Liverpool to win. That's it, basically.

'Klopp is Liverpool's one hope regarding Wirtz'

However, Carragher feels Wirtz could be saved by former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp during the international break.

Klopp has selected Wirtz for Germany's upcoming Nations League games. Wirtz has been named in one of two separate Germany squads chosen by Klopp and the Liverpool midfielder will get a rest before being in contention to feature in Die Mannschaft's last two games against Serbia and Greece.

"The one hope for Liverpool supporters now is Jurgen Klopp is the Germany manager," said Carragher.

"Wirtz goes away with the Germany team for three weeks, and he's obviously one of the best players in Germany, that's how they see him. Can Jurgen Klopp sprinkle a bit of stardust on him in that position?

"Jurgen is one of the greatest managers in the world, we know that. And what he gets out of players is probably more than most managers because of the nature of his personality, and fingers crossed something can happen for him.

"There's a scenario there that Jurgen Klopp and Germany have a great international window, he gets loads of goals, assists and comes back on a high. Manchester City's the next game, he impacts that, all is forgotten, all is forgiven. There's a potential turnaround there.

"I would love that to happen, I'd love him to be the match-winner against Manchester City."

articles.title: Alvaro Arbeloa accuses officials of not wanting Manchester United to lose after late controversy in draw at Fulham
articles.summary: Man Utd rescued a late 1-1 draw at Fulham after Matheus Cunha's deflected equaliser; Alvaro Arbeloa felt Harry Maguire winning a free-kick 35 seconds before the equaliser for a 'foul' by Cesar Palacios was soft; Arbeloa felt the refs were kinder to United after the Manchester derby drama
articles.body:
United rescued a 1-1 draw after Matheus Cunha scored a deflected 89th-minute equaliser - but Fulham head coach Arbeloa was furious that, 35 seconds before the goal, United were given a free-kick for a foul on Harry Maguire on the halfway line.

Arbeloa felt the free-kick for Cesar Palacios' foul on Maguire was soft and claimed referee Michael Oliver and his team of officials gave "all fouls" to United - because of the "error in judgement" by the officials who incorrectly awarded Erling Haaland's Manchester derby winner at Old Trafford last weekend.

"All fouls for them," Arbeloa told Sky Sports. "You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire, he's a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them.

"And I knew. I knew after the game against Man City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here. We deserved a little bit more.

"We were so close. So, so close. We were a little bit unlucky again. We knew it would be difficult against this big team.

"Also we knew what happened last week. We have seen what the referees have been doing all the match so it was a difficult game. And we were unlucky."

In his press conference, Arbeloa appeared to row back on his comments a little bit - but still said he "was not really happy".

"My English is not so good," he said. "Maybe I explain myself so bad and I prefer not to say anything about the referees because you never know.

"When you say something that you don't have to say, it's better to stay calm, focus on the performance of my team and focus on the next game.

"I'm not really happy. Like I said, I need to be focused and put my energy in all the things that I have to improve.

"[Maguire] is a very big guy and maybe it wasn't a foul. But it's ok. Like I said, I prefer to analyse the game - players, systems and it's the best for win.

"You know when you draw a game like that, maybe you're a little bit frustrated."

Is it a foul? Young and Saha analyse the decision

Analysing the Maguire foul on Super Sunday, former Manchester United defender Ashley Young told Sky Sports: "It's definitely a foul. Palacios isn't looking at the ball, he's straight into Maguire's back.

"I know he [Arbeola] says Maguire is 100kg, but he's smart, he's waiting for the foul to be committed."

Asked if it was a foul, former Fulham and Manchester United forward Louis Saha added: "It is.

"It might be soft, but that's where some players have experience, they use their body in the right way. In his position, he [Maguire] felt like he couldn't take the control so it was a clever piece of work from Maguire."

Should Man Utd have been given penalty for Bassey handball?

Another talking point came just before United's equaliser - when Fulham defender Calvin Bassey was accused of handball after Lisandro Martinez's ball forward into the penalty area.

VAR looked at the decision but agreed with the assistant referee's view that Bassey had his arm close to his body - even though it struck his hand.

"He did put his hand up," said Gary Neville on co-commentary. "The fact that the hand is close to the body might save him."

Analysing the decision, Saha said: "Its kind of a 50:50, you don't know now with the rules. It hits his hand. The natural instinct you have is to protect your face because you know you're going to be hit.

"It's different rules every weekend, we don't understand it. Some will blow, some will go on."

Image: The officials did not give a penalty for this handball by Calvin Bassey

articles.title: Jose Mourinho: Real Madrid boss holds up pictures of referee errors in press conference after defeat to Atletico Madrid
articles.summary: Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho held up pictures of refereeing errors following 2-1 defeat to Atletico Madrid; Mourinho claimed referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias couldnt cope with the pressure; he claimed Cristian Romero and Lee Kang-in should have both been sent off
articles.body:
Mourinho strongly criticised the officials and was angry that Atletico defender Cristian Romero ‌ was not sent off for a stamp on Jude Bellingham .

He also complained about a challenge by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde , before the visitors were reduced to 10 men five minutes after half-time.

"We could skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," ​Mourinho said, holding up the images in what was the start of a near ‌five-minute rant.

"Those were two clear red cards. The difficulties we've faced since the sending-off - 11 against 10 - well, we can imagine what 50 ​minutes of 11 against nine would have been like if justice had been done."

Real defender Dean Huijsen was dismissed for bringing down Giuliano Simeone inside the area as the last defender, allowing Alejandro Grimaldo to ​score with a low spot-kick.

Jonathan David doubled Atletico's lead six minutes later, ⁠with Antonio Rudiger heading in a free-kick late ⁠to reduce the deficit.

Mourinho said he could only "hug" his players after what he described as a first half "full of class and great character", but he aimed sharp ‌criticism at referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias and those who appointed him.

"They've put a referee, aged 41, with no international experience - it's certainly not because he's a great referee," Mourinho said.

"Then the poor chap has come ‌here and hasn't been able to cope with the pressure - and it really is intense pressure. I call it '80s-style pressure' here in this stadium, which you hardly ever see these days."

Asked about being six points behind Barcelona, Mourinho offered a pointed reply.

"If they just leave us in peace and let us compete on a level playing field ⁠with everyone else, we've still got a long way to go," he said.

"I don't ​want to go so far as to say this was set up... I ​want to believe that they simply made a mistake."

'A derby marked by poor officiating,' say Real Madrid

Real Madrid released an official match report after full-time which echoed the views of Mourinho.

The La Liga club claimed the defeat was "marked by poor officiating".

"Real Madrid lost at the Metropolitano in a derby marked by the poor officiating of Ortiz Arias, who failed to send off Cuti Romero in the first half for stepping on Jude Bellingham's knee (despite reviewing the play on the monitor) and Kang-In Lee for stepping on Valverde's left ankle.

"Both decisions shaped the match, which was decided in the second half in favor of Atletico.

"Until the 30th minute, the game had very few dangerous plays. But from that point on, controversy took over the derby.

"In the 35th minute, during a contested ball, Bellingham got to the ball before Cuti Romero, and the Atletico defender planted his studs into the left knee of the Madrid player. Ortiz Arias initially booked our player but was called by Trujillo Suarez to review the incident on the monitor.

"After watching the replay, he rescinded the card from Bellingham and issued a yellow card to the Atletico defender instead of sending him off.

"Nine minutes later, the referee made another crucial error by not penalizing Kang-In Lee for a challenge on Valverde, where he struck him with his studs on the left ankle.

"Ortiz Arias was close to the incident but did not show a red card (or even a yellow card) to the Atlético player, nor was he alerted by Trujillo Suárez on this occasion."

Image: Real Madrid's Jude Bellingham and Atletico Madrid's Cristian Romero grimace on the ground after a collision during the derby

articles.title: Martin O'Neill to consider Celtic future as Rangers defeat adds to growing scrutiny | 'Might be time to wrap it up'
articles.summary: Celtic lost 1-0 to Rangers in the Scottish Premiership, a week after their League Cup exit against their Old Firm rivals; Martin O'Neill's side lost 3-1 at home to Ferencvaros in their Europa League opener between those defeats to Derek McInnes' side; Celtic are two points clear of Rangers
articles.body:
The Light Blues cruised to a 3-0 League Cup win over the Hoops at Ibrox last Sunday and, in the Scottish Premiership rematch, a first-half strike by Ryan Naderi took Derek McInnes' side to within two points of the Hoops at the top of the table going into the international break.

In his second spell as permanent manager after two stints as interim boss last season, O'Neill was under growing pressure going into the game after the 3-1 loss to Ferencvaros at Parkhead on Thursday night .

Following another poor performance, the 74-year-old spoke about entering a period of self-reflection.

"I genuinely will reflect and see," the Northern Irishman said. "It's a matter of whether I can help the team. The manager is supposed to be able to do that. I will look at that this week.

"I think every single time something crops up and things don't go so well, age plays a part. And, do you know what, they might be right. I'll be 110 in two years' time so it might be time to wrap it up.

"I will reflect on the games and speak to the board. You never know, they may well want to speak to me. I'll try to get a couple of days away and see how it goes."

Asked what would happen if he reflected, then decided he could not improve the team, O'Neill replied: "By that time, I will promise you, I'll let you know.

O'Neill addressed the growing negativity within the Hoops support, saying: "Well, I think they're absolutely entitled.

"I mentioned this to you on Friday, absolutely entitled to, of course.

"And I'm not immune from criticism. Far from it. Absolutely and utterly far from it.

"I think there's every reason to ask, 'can you turn this round? Can you change the whole thing?'

"We are, as I said, two points clear, so I have to kind of look at the bigger picture at this minute.

"But I knew that we were in a big, big fight anyway, with both ourselves, Rangers, and Hearts again, who are far from out of anything.

"It's a long season ahead. It's not the first time I've been questioned about my managerial time. So, yeah, I'll have a look at it. I will reflect and see."

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Sky Sports:

"He's [Martin O'Neill] changed formation, he made four changes midweek. He's trying to find a recipe to get some fluidity.

"Rangers were the far superior team, not just in physical attributes and running power, but football.

"They played all the football. Celtic were a lot better than they have been in the first half, without being brilliant.

"But second half, totally disjointed, totally outplayed. Outworked, which is the worst thing you can label at a team. Really disjointed, battered, actually battered.

"All the best players were in a blue shirt today. Celtic have a lot to ponder and a lot to work out.

"They've got an international break, which is probably coming at a good time for them. I know a lot of them may be away playing for their countries but there needs to be a total reset because the last three performances in the space of a week have been very poor."

"Knowing Martin, he'll be greatly concerned. I don't like to disagree with him but it wasn't a close game. There was a massive gulf between the teams.

"I can't actually remember a Celtic team getting such a doing at Celtic Park from a Rangers team, which happened today.

"It looked like Celtic were making it up as they went along. Rangers were better in every department.

"Celtic have got big problems. They were smashed by Rangers and that's a concern."

articles.title: Crítica salvaje de una leyenda del Liverpool a Wirtz: "Iraola tiene que tomar una decisión aquí"
articles.standfirst: Jamie Carragher se mostró preocupado con el nivel del alemán desde su llegada hace dos veranos
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher se mostró preocupado con el nivel del alemán desde su llegada hace dos veranos
articles.body: Jamie Carragher, leyenda del Liverpool, no se mordió la lengua con Florian Wirtz el pasado fin de semana. El exjugador del Liverpool fue especialmente duro con el alemán en su podcast tras la victoria ante el Bournemouth en un partido en el que uno de los fichajes estrella de los ‘reds’ en los últimos años volvió a dejar una actuación por debajo de las expectativas. El equipo de Iraola ganó gracias al gol de Alexander Isak, pero Wirtz fue sustituido en la segunda mitad y volvió a quedar señalado. La crítica adquiere todavía más peso por el contexto. Wirtz llegó a Anfield como uno de los grandes objetos de deseo del fútbol europeo después de su espectacular etapa en el Bayer Leverkusen. Liverpool se impuso en una carrera en la que también aparecieron otros grandes clubes y pagó 100 millones de libras fijos más 16,5 en variables, lo que puede convertir la operación en 116,5 millones, lo que le convierte en el tercer fichaje más caro de la historia de la Premier, solo por detrás de Morgan Rogers e Isak. Precisamente por eso, Carragher entiende que el alemán está ofreciendo demasiado poco. "Fue una de las peores actuaciones que le he visto con la camiseta del Liverpool", aseguró, antes de ir todavía más lejos: "Pero la razón por la que estoy preocupado es que no creo que Wirtz esté en mal momento desde que llegó al Liverpool. En realidad, creo que lo que vemos es su verdadero nivel". El exdefensa incidió también en la diferencia entre el jugador que deslumbró en Alemania y el que está apareciendo en Liverpool. "Normalmente, cuando ves a Wirtz, encuentras a un jugador elegante y ordenado, que conserva el balón, y hay cosas que te gustan de él. Sale de situaciones difíciles en las que normalmente esperarías que tu jugador perdiera el balón", explicó. Pero, en su opinión, ni siquiera esas virtudes están teniendo impacto suficiente ahora mismo: "No veo cómo va a hacer daño". Y Carragher terminó poniendo sobre la mesa una medida drástica: sentar al futbolista. "Iraola tiene que tomar una decisión aquí. Wirtz no estaría en mi equipo en el Liverpool a día de hoy", sentenció.

articles.title: Raúl Varela: "Mourinho es el gran perdedor del domingo"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu señala al técnico portugués tras la derrota en el derbi y advierte del peligro para el Real Madrid: "Tener una excusa veraz para no hacer autocrítica"
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu señala al técnico portugués tras la derrota en el derbi y advierte del peligro para el Real Madrid: "Tener una excusa veraz para no hacer autocrítica"
articles.body: Raúl Varela analizó en La Tribu el derbi del Metropolitano y resumió el encuentro señalando a tres nombres propios. El periodista puso el foco en Ortiz Arias, Giuliano Simeone y José Mourinho para explicar el 2-1 y una derrota del Real Madrid que, a su juicio, deja también una lectura sobre la situación de los tres grandes: "Hoy, el Barça está muchos cuerpos por delante de sus dos perseguidores". Varela comenzó su análisis recurriendo a Gareth Bale para resumir lo sucedido: "Si en vez de Raúl Varela me llamase Gareth Bale el titular que resumiría el derbi del Metropolitano de ayer estaría chupado. 'Ortiz Arias, Giuliano Simeone y José Mourinho, in that order'". El primero de los señalados fue el colegiado. Varela fue muy crítico con su actuación: "La designación de Ortiz Arias explicada a través del padrón municipal y nunca por el rendimiento estaba condenada al fracaso como así fue". Y añadió: "El pobre no acertó ni equivocándose". El periodista enumeró varias acciones que, a su juicio, marcaron el arbitraje: "Indultó a Kang In Lee al filo del descanso con una sonrisa, ¿de qué se ríen los árbitros?, en la misma cara de Valverde que ha resultado lesionado por dos semanas. Amonestó a Bellingham en la acción en la que debió expulsar al Cuti, perdonó a Huijsen hasta que le corrigieron la roja que se enseña en el colegio de aprendices". Después apareció Giuliano Simeone. Varela destacó su influencia en el derbi pese a que el Atlético comenzó la segunda mitad con once futbolistas: "Giuliano se encargó de multiplicarse, para que nadie diga, y bailó unas cuantas veces a la defensa madridista". También dejó una de sus frases más contundentes: "Sí, el hijo del jefe que se lleva en su culo las patadas que no se atreven a dar algunos en el pompis de su padre". Varela también apuntó directamente al rendimiento de varios jugadores madridistas: "Cucurella pasó su peor tarde blanco y Huijsen volvió a enseñarnos lo que vio De la Fuente antes de ir al campeonato del mundo, que al igual que le ocurre a Güler cuando juegan contra los mayores están más crudos que un sashimi". El tercer gran protagonista de su análisis fue José Mourinho, al que Varela calificó como "el gran perdedor de este domingo". El periodista recordó las dudas que ya había planteado sobre qué versión del técnico portugués iba a encontrarse el Real Madrid: "¿Qué Mourinho íbamos a ver? ¿Un estratega? ¿Un agente polémico? ¿El brazo ejecutor de un presidente molesto por la lista de invitados al palco? ¿Un entrenador superado por la modernidad?". Para Varela, el problema para el conjunto blanco tras la derrota puede estar precisamente en encontrar una explicación externa que evite mirar hacia dentro: "Al Madrid le ha pasado lo peor que le podía pasar. Tener una excusa veraz para no hacer autocrítica después de una derrota merecida". El periodista cerró su reflexión repasando algunos de los síntomas que dejó el encuentro: "Mbappé, el del Balón de Oro, acabó sacando córners, a Vinicius ya le enseñan la puerta de salida, y hasta Courtois se ha hecho humano. Por eso, la lista de errores versión 2026". Y terminó regresando a la referencia británica con la que había arrancado: "Como diría ese proverbio tan británico como Gareth Bale: cuando señalas con un dedo hay otros tres que apuntan hacia ti".

articles.title: Un problema interminable: el mapa de calor de Vinicius y Mbappé en el derbi que preocupa al madridismo
articles.standfirst: Ambos cracks, desaparecidos en el Metropolitano, volvieron prácticamente a calcar su radio de acción -por la izquierda- en otro partido grande
articles.summary: Ambos cracks, desaparecidos en el Metropolitano, volvieron prácticamente a calcar su radio de acción -por la izquierda- en otro partido grande
articles.body: El derbi del Metropolitano volvió a dejar muchas preguntas en el Real Madrid. El 2-1 ante el Atlético no solo dejó la derrota y la rajada de Mourinho sobre el arbitraje: también volvió a poner sobre la mesa un problema que acompaña al equipo desde hace tiempo y que se hizo especialmente visible en el comportamiento de sus dos grandes estrellas. Vinicius y Mbappé vuelven a 'pisarse'. El mapa de calor de ambos durante el partido resulta revelador. Vinicius aparece muy concentrado en el sector izquierdo, como es habitual en él, pero también ocupando zonas interiores. Mbappé, por su parte, nace a priori como delantero en el 1-4-2-3-1 de Mou, aunque su radio de acción se extiende también hacia la izquierda. El resultado es una importante acumulación de los dos en los mismos espacios. Lo de siempre. No es una cuestión nueva, ni mucho menos. Vinicius y Mbappé, desde la llegada del astro francés hace dos años, parecen condenados a 'no entenderse', con sus momentos de forma tendían a coincidir en sentido contrario: cuando uno despega, el otro se atasca. Y así con cuatro entrenadores -Ancelotti, Xabi, Arbeloa y Mourinho- diferentes. En el Metropolitano, además, ninguno consiguió convertir esa convivencia en producción ofensiva. El Madrid terminó con apenas 0,32 de goles esperados, su registro más bajo en un partido de Liga desde febrero de 2015, según los datos de Opta. Mbappé solo realizó un disparo y Vinicius, dos, pero fue sustituido en el minuto 54. Un problema que, además, viene escenificado en la semana en la que Zinedine Zidane, nuevo seleccionador francés, dejó caer en su primera rueda de prensa previa al parón de combinados nacionales que le gusta mucho Kylian partiendo desde la izquierda. De hecho, fuentes galas como RMC Sport hablan de que el técnico incluso ya ha llamado al jugador del Real Madrid para comunicarle que, con él, jugará en esta posición. Un problema interminable que apunta a seguir en boca del madridismo tras la dolorosa caída en el derbi y que ahora coincide con un mal momento del equipo... y sobre todo del brasileño, con Yan Diomande llamando a la puerta tras ser de lo poco 'potable' del equipo en una nueva derrota en el Metropolitano. La pelota, de primeras, está en el tejado de Mourinho.

After opening their campaign with a 19-0 demolition of Uzbekistan, the Women in Blue have now scored 36 goals in two matches, underlining their dominance in the tournament.Forwards Deepika Sehrawat, Rutuja Dadaso Pisal and Navneet Kaur each scored a hat-trick as India registered their second consecutive win. The victory also saw veteran goalkeeper Savita Punia make history by becoming the most-capped player in Indian women’s hockey, with her 321st senior international appearance.India dominate from the startThe 2023 Asian Games bronze medallists came out firing at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium, scoring four goals in the opening quarter before adding five more in the second to take a commanding 9-0 lead at half-time.India maintained the pressure after the break, scoring five more goals in the third quarter and adding three in the final 15 minutes. Indonesia managed a consolation goal in the third quarter, but it did little to slow India’s attacking momentum.The win took India to six points from two Pool B matches, with a goal difference of 35.Deepika, Rutuja and Navneet hit hat-tricksDeepika, Rutuja and Navneet led India’s scoring with three goals each. Deepika continued her impressive form after scoring eight goals against Uzbekistan in the tournament opener.Sunelita Toppo, Lalremsiami and Sakshi Rana contributed two goals apiece, while captain Salima Tete and Ishika Chaudhary also found the net. India opened the scoring through Deepika’s penalty-corner conversion in the eighth minute. Sunelita and Lalremsiami added goals before Rutuja scored in the closing moments of the first quarter.The Indian forwards continued to find openings in the second quarter, extending the lead to 9-0 by half-time. Indonesia scored through Innes Adiyita in the third quarter, but India responded quickly and kept piling on the goals.Savita Punia sets new Indian women’s hockey recordThe match was also a landmark occasion for Savita Punia, who earned her 321st senior international cap to become the most-capped player in Indian women’s hockey history. The former India captain moved past Vandana Katariya, who held the previous record with 320 appearances. Savita’s milestone adds to a career that has seen her represent India at multiple major international tournaments.India face Thailand nextIndia will next take on Thailand in their third Pool B match on Wednesday as they look to maintain their winning run at the Asian Games.
